evidence.headline: Preview 6 build, package and emulator checks
evidence.framing: Preview 6 preserves queued input age and pending loss feedback. Earlier Preview 3 playback results are historical; physical-device and Internet gameplay acceptance for Preview 6 remain pending.
evidence.scope: Matching {{RELEASE_LABEL}} Windows, Android and Linux viewer packages
items: Optimized Windows desktop and host builds, signed Android ARM64/x86_64 builds and release lint, and the Linux viewer build passed.
Package checks validated embedded versions, Android signature and archive structure, and updater hashes. All seven public assets matched their local SHA-256.
Local input and feedback regressions cover queue dwell, partial and rejected sends, and loss-ID retention. They do not measure gameplay latency.
The signed release APK executed pointer and scroll JNI calls and rejected input without a session on an Android API 36 x86_64 emulator.
All platforms share production source d801732. The release source tag adds only instrumentation and acceptance documentation; the release includes build provenance.
caveats: Use Preview 6 on both ends for the latest remote-input fixes. Remote-input protocol remains version 3.
The emulator check does not establish ARM64 runtime, physical controller/game compatibility, Internet input-to-photon latency or video quality under congestion.
Person cards, menus and the Blocked list have not been checked on a physical Android device, touch hardware or a screen reader.
The Blocked list appears once the hosted comms service is updated; until then it stays empty.
Audible microphone/speaker quality, physical Linux playback and screen sharing between unrelated networks remain unverified. These are not glass-to-glass latency measurements.
Update every group participant: older unsigned group invitations are rejected.
Windows is unsigned; Android is debug-signed. Linux requires a compatible desktop, ALSA and GStreamer.

capability_groups.title: Sending and watching
capability_groups.intro: Included screen-sharing features, with device requirements and testing results.

items.name: Screen and window capture
items.detail: Share an entire screen, or pick a single window, from a Windows x64 PC.

items.name: Video quality controls
items.detail: Choose source size or a 480p, 720p, 1080p, 1440p or 2160p resolution limit, 30 or 60 fps, and 1â€“50 Mb/s. The 5 Mbps Wi-Fi preset uses 720p, 30 fps and a 3 Mb/s video ceiling. Reduced resolution uses CPU encoding; sustained 60 fps depends on the PC.

items.name: H.264 encoding
items.detail: Windows shares H.264 using the available encoder. Hardware support and CPU cost vary; this build has not been validated on every vendor.

items.name: Android receiving
items.detail: Android 8 or newer receives screens using its decoder. S25 Ultra playback, full-screen pinch zoom and rotation were checked on this release. ARM64 and x86-64 libraries are included; other devices remain unqualified.

items.name: Windows receiving
items.detail: A second Windows PC can receive the screen and system audio. Both ends need matching builds.

items.name: Computer audio
items.detail: The sending PC can include system audio with its screen. Audible output and endurance remain unverified for this build.

items.name: Linux x64 receiving
items.detail: Separate viewer package for Ubuntu 24.04 or compatible desktops with ALSA and GStreamer 1.22+. No Linux screen broadcasting; physical playback and audio acceptance pending.

capability_groups.title: Features awaiting physical validation
capability_groups.intro: These features are included, but physical-device tests remain outstanding.

items.name: Person cards and actions
items.detail: Every place a person appears opens the same card, with the same actions from right-click, long-press or Shift+F10. Remove friend and Block ask first. Windows and Android share one set of rules. Physical touch and screen-reader checks remain open.

items.name: Blocked list and unblocking
items.detail: Lists the people you blocked so you can unblock them. Needs the updated hosted comms service; until it is deployed the list stays empty.

items.name: Private session admission
items.detail: The viewing device issues a private invitation that authorises the session over a pinned QUIC connection. Expiry, replay, and revocation pass loopback tests; physical regression testing is still open.

items.name: Two-way microphone voice
items.detail: One-to-one and group calls use direct peer paths with relay fallback and authenticated sender identities. A phone/desktop group probe passed with generated audio; physical microphone, echo and network-handoff checks remain outstanding. Update all participants.

items.name: Remote control from Android
items.detail: Android receives screens. It does not currently provide the account proof required by named-account remote-control grants, so those sessions remain view-only.

items.name: Cursor appearance and effects
items.detail: Desktop cursor styling with a local effects budget. The current build labels this preview only.

items.name: Several viewers on one share
items.detail: One Windows capture can serve up to eight independently admitted viewers. Windows Tables subscribe to up to four live friend screens and support late joins. Physical multi-device acceptance remains open.

items.name: Sharing a screen during a call
items.detail: A call and a screen share can run together. Accepted Windows friends discover live Table shares automatically after the sender explicitly starts sharing.

items.name: Windows Table layout and fullscreen
items.detail: Seats resize from every edge and corner. Settings are menus; fullscreen hides the surrounding UI. Interactive acceptance remains open.

items.name: Profile pictures
items.detail: Windows and Android support choosing, changing and removing profile pictures. Android uses explicit Save and Discard controls.

items.name: In-call text and files
items.detail: Windows and Android include session chat and consent-based file transfer. Files require a direct route; session chat is not a durable offline archive.

items.name: Automatic update checks
items.detail: Matched downloads include the Windows and Android preview update manifest. Windows installer lifecycle and Android signing continuity passed; automatic update prompts still need physical acceptance.

capability_groups.title: Features with additional limitations
capability_groups.intro: Internet playback remains unqualified, and accounts and contacts have local-storage limitations.

items.name: Viewing outside your local network
items.detail: Direct routes are preferred and the Pyrenet relay provides fallback. This build includes negotiation and route-repair fixes, but unrelated-network physical acceptance remains open.

items.name: Device-owned accounts and contacts
items.detail: Device-held keys identify accounts. The coordination service supports profiles, friends and invitations; it is not a fully decentralized account service.

capability_groups.title: Not in this download
capability_groups.intro: The following features are not included in {{RELEASE_LABEL}}.

items.name: macOS, iPhone, and iPad
items.detail: Not implemented. This preview download is Windows x64, Android 8 or newer and a Linux x64 viewer. Android does not send.

limitations: Windows binaries are unsigned; Android is debug-signed. Update every group participant to this version.
Windows-to-S25 Ultra playback was checked on a controlled 5 Mbps path. Capture timing still varies; audible media, physical Linux playback and unrelated-network screen sharing remain unverified.
Direct connections minimize relay traffic; relay fallback still uses relay bandwidth.
Bulk file transfers require a direct route and explicit acceptance; they do not use relay fallback.
Networks blocking all UDP have no call/media fallback. Persistent room discussions use the coordination service.
Automatic Table viewing is view-only. Named-account remote control currently requires a compatible Windows viewer.
Android receives screens and supports calls/chat; Android screen broadcasting is not implemented.
No owner/process migration or durable offline peer chat is provided.
macOS, iPhone, iPad and browser apps are not available.
Linux is viewer-only and dynamically linked; use Ubuntu 24.04 or a compatible desktop with ALSA and GStreamer 1.22+.

Windows room voice channels have hosted coordination support. Shared viewer cursors and measured multi-device latency remain unfinished. Search covers loaded messages in one selected conversation, not a global index.

history.label: 0.4.0 Preview 6
history.summary: Desktop feedback retains loss IDs omitted from compact packets. Desktop and Android pointer and scroll paths preserve queued sample age. Matched Windows, Android and Linux viewer packages; packaged JNI checks passed on an x86_64 Android emulator. Physical gameplay and Internet latency remain unverified.

history.label: 0.4.0 Preview 5
history.summary: Remote-play input and recovery improvements: reliable controller button transitions, stale-input expiry, bounded interactive queues and persistent video repair requests. Windows, Android and Linux viewer packages; physical gameplay and Internet latency remain unverified.

history.label: 0.4.0 Preview 4
history.summary: Person cards with the same actions everywhere (right-click, long-press, Shift+F10), confirmed Remove friend and Block, a Blocked list, Table seat actions, the Android person sheet, and desktop menus sized and placed like other chat apps. Matching Windows, Android and Linux viewer packages; the hosted service is unchanged, so the Blocked list stays empty until it is updated.

history.label: 0.4.0 Preview 3

Hosted services and matching Windows, Android and Linux viewer packages updated.
